meanings: (Buddhism) to free oneself of worldly worries

components.note: 角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'
⺼ (flesh, body) — 脱 relates to taking something off the body.
兑 (duì) gives a sound close to tuō, sharing a related initial.
忄 (heart, mind) — 懦 (cowardly, weak-willed) is a trait seated in the heart.
需 (xū) gives a sound only distantly related to nuò today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'
责 shows 贝 (money, a cowry shell) at its base, tied to a debt that must be repaid — giving 责 its meaning 'duty, responsibility, to blame.'
纟 (thread) — 终 originally referred to the end of a woven thread, extended to mean 'end, final'
冬 (dōng) gives a loose sound connection to 终's reading zhōng
纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.
八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'
西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
隹 (short-tailed bird) — 雅 originally named a type of crow, later borrowed for the unrelated meaning 'elegant, refined.'
牙 (yá) gives a sound close to yǎ, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.
图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
犭 (dog) — 狂 originally described a mad, rabid dog, extending to 'wild, crazy.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to kuáng, having drifted apart over time.
灬 (fire) — 热 relates directly to heat
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 热's reading rè

meanings: to provide financial or material support

兟 (shēn) gives a sound distantly related to zàn, having drifted apart over time.
力 (strength) — 助 relates to helping, lending one's strength
且 (qiě) gives a loose sound connection to 助's reading zhù
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
土 depicts a mound of earth resting on the ground — a simple picture of soil, giving 土 its meaning 'earth, soil, land.'
The bowl-shaped body of an old stemmed serving dish.
A lid or rim on top of the dish.
亲 (here representing a tree, related to 榛/hazel) — 新 pictures a tree being cut.
斤 (an axe) — freshly chopping wood gave 新 its meaning of something 'new' or 'fresh.'
氵 (water) — 泽 names a marsh or pool, a body of water.
西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
衣 (cloth) — 裂 describes cloth tearing apart.
列 (liè) is an exact match for the sound of 裂.
Thread — sewing uses thread.
Gives the sound féng, matching the character's other reading (as a verb meaning 'to sew').
工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.
禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.
亻 (person) — 偶 originally described a wooden figure or idol shaped like a person, later extending to 'a pair' and 'by chance.'
禺 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to 偶's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.
灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.
火 (fire) — 烦 describes a burning, irritated feeling.
页 (yè) gives a sound distantly related to fán, having drifted apart over time.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

無-shaped top pictures a dancer holding decorated sleeves or fans.
舛 below pictures a pair of feet, together giving 舞 its meaning 'to dance.'
亻 (person) — 伴 describes a person accompanying another.
半 (bàn) is an exact match for the sound of 伴.
一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'
土 (earth) — 堕 describes falling down toward the ground.
陏 (Suí) gives a sound distantly related to duò, having drifted apart over time.
艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match
羽 (feather) — a wing is covered in feathers.
支 (zhī) gives a sound fairly close to chì, sharing a similar rhyme.
⺼ (flesh) — 膀 names a part of the body.
旁 (beside) contributes to the character's form, describing something at the body's side, like the upper arm or a wing.
丹 depicts a pellet of red cinnabar mineral, dug from a mine — the source of its meaning 'cinnabar, red, pellet.'
手 (hand) — 掌 names the palm, part of the hand.
尚 (shàng) gives a rhyme close to zhǎng, with the initial shifted.
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.
王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 瑞 describes a jade tablet used as a token of good fortune.
耑 (duān) gives a sound distantly related to ruì, having drifted apart over time.
纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.
尸 (a body) — the body of an animal.
毛 (fur/hair) — trailing behind it, together giving 尾 its meaning 'tail.'
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'
页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) gives a sound close to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
米 (rice) — the grain being measured.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring out rice gave 料 its meaning 'material, to estimate, to reckon.'
高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
辶 (to walk/move) — 速 relates to the speed of movement
束 (shù) gives a loose sound connection to 速's reading sù

meanings: variant of 贊同|赞同[zan4 tong2]

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赞 originally related to offering valuables in support of someone.
兟 (shēn) gives a sound distantly related to zàn, having drifted apart over time.
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'

meanings: variant of 合併|合并[he2 bing4]

components.note: 并 (simplified from 並) depicts two people standing side by side — giving its meaning of 'together' or 'and.'
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time
乂 (a hand holding a writing tool) — the act of recording events, giving 史 its meaning 'history, chronicle.'
艹 (plant) — 蒂 names the stem that attaches a fruit or flower to its plant.
帝 (dì) gives the sound — an exact match with 蒂.
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'
大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.
亻 (person) — 伊 originally referred to a person
尹 (yǐn) gives a sound close to 伊's reading yī, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
丽 is the simplified form of 麗, which depicted the ornate antlers of a deer (鹿) — a fitting image behind its meaning 'beautiful, magnificent.'
艹 (grass) — 莎 originally named a type of sedge grass.
沙 (shā) gives the sound — an exact match with 莎.
Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'
玉 (jade, shown without its dot) represents something valuable.
厶 beneath suggests something slipping away privately, giving 丢 its meaning 'to lose, to throw away.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'
土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match

贝 (money/shell) — a heavy load of money the person is carrying on their back
责 shows 贝 (money, a cowry shell) at its base, tied to a debt that must be repaid — giving 责 its meaning 'duty, responsibility, to blame.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
贝 (shell/money) — 费 relates to spending money, fees, and expenses
弗 (fú) gives a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi
木 (wood) — 极 originally named the ridgepole, the highest beam of a roof, extended to 'extreme, utmost.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 极 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.
立 (to stand) — 端 relates to standing upright, being straight and proper.

meanings: intern (esp. a student in practical training)

components.note: 屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
一 (one) is used here as a simple graphic base for the character.
从 (cóng) gives the exact sound of 丛.
木 (tree), doubled — two trees side by side depict a cluster of trees, the source of 林's meaning 'forest, grove.'
口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.
讠 (speech) — the act of speaking.
正 (straight, correct) — speaking the straight, correct truth, giving 证 its meaning 'to prove, certify; evidence.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.
刂 (a knife, related to 刀) — cutting and arranging pieces in order ties to 列's meaning 'row, line, to arrange'
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
